title: Per-task git worktrees: parallel work on shared files, landing to main
description:
Human decision, 2026-10-30 ("3 everything going to main"), in answer to the governor's throughput analysis.

Today every seat edits ONE shared checkout, and the wrappers land whole files onto the shared moe/work-<date> branch. That forces architects to chain every pair of tasks that touch the same file via dependsOn. On 2026-10-30, 38 of 49 live rows were dependency-gated, and the longest chain was 16 rows. The cost shows up several ways:
- About 8 edges exist only because two tasks share a file.
- Contested-landing tangles happened, for example R11e2 and 2cf1c6be in scripts/tests/local-runner.test.mjs.
- Codex, Grok and Gemini seats can't land contested paths (task-9d277494).
- Every seat hot-reloads a peer's half-edited moe-agent.sh (task-5998f871).

Deliver this:
1. Each claimed task runs in its own git worktree on its own branch, cut from the current main.
2. The wrapper lands the task by rebasing it onto main and updating main with a compare-and-swap after the task's gate passes, so non-overlapping hunks in the same file merge automatically.
3. A true conflict parks the bytes on a rescue ref and routes the task back for a rebase, never a silent overwrite.
4. Everything lands on main. The moe/work-<date> consolidation branch and the "never commit on main" peel rule are retired for worktree mode.
5. Once that is live, architects stop chaining tasks that only share a file, so idle seats can take parallel rows.
architectureNotes:
Starting points (verify against the code before planning; nothing here is a landed contract):
- Landing today: scripts/moe-agent.{sh,ps1} post-flight builds a temp index, then commit-tree, then an update-ref CAS onto settings.consolidationBranch (else moe/work-<date>). Inside a private worktree, every dirty byte belongs to that task, so the baseline, PLANNED, MEASURED and CONTESTED tiers can collapse. Decide explicitly what survives, because the DENY and BOARD rules still matter.
- .moe/ runtime state is daemon-owned and lives in the MAIN checkout. Worktrees must never carry or write .moe runtime. Board records (.moe/tasks/<id>.json) need a decision: commit them from the main checkout, or stop committing them per task.
- Seats must run the wrapper from committed bytes, not from a task worktree (see task-5998f871).
- Per-worktree tooling: the Serena project root, node_modules and dist builds (daemon/proxy tests need a build), the Gradle lease for JetBrains, and .worktrees/** is already in DENY.
- Gates (settings.qualityGate) run inside the task worktree, against the rebased tree that will actually land.
- Conflict policy: on a rebase conflict, land nothing, park the bytes on refs/moe/rescue/<task>/..., and route the task back. Never auto-resolve.
- Rollout behind a setting (e.g. settings.worktreeMode). Keep the shared-checkout mode working until this epic's final task flips the default.
- After rollout, sweep dependsOn edges that exist only for file overlap; the governor's 2026-10-30 audit lists them.
epicRails: Main is only ever updated by a compare-and-swap ref update after the task's gate passes; never force-push or rewrite main's history.
Keep scripts/moe-agent.sh and scripts/moe-agent.ps1 in parity; bash scripts/tests/parity-check.sh must pass on every task.
The daemon stays the sole writer of .moe/ runtime state; worktrees never contain or write .moe runtime files.
Shared-checkout mode keeps working, unchanged, until the epic's final task switches the default.
